meta.description: My Florence guide: the six hotels I'd stay at and why, the after-hours experiences most visitors never see, and what I'd tell a friend before they go.

stay.deck: One for every kind of Florence trip. These are the hotels I send friends to.

perks.text: Fora perks line goes here — e.g. an upgrade when available, daily breakfast and a hotel credit when you book through me. Keith to supply exact wording.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Firenze
hotels.alt: The frescoed courtyard of the Renaissance palazzo at Four Seasons Hotel Firenze
hotels.take: A Renaissance palazzo inside a private garden that feels impossible this close to the Duomo. It’s the only hotel in Florence that gives you a resort and the city in the same stay, and the service is the most polished in town.

hotels.name: Portrait Firenze
hotels.alt: A river-view suite at Portrait Firenze looking onto the Ponte Vecchio
hotels.take: Suites right on the Arno, so the Ponte Vecchio is out your window rather than down the street. The rooms are apartment-sized, which matters more than you’d think after a long museum day. Ask for a river view; that’s the whole point.

hotels.name: The Place
hotels.alt: The Place Firenze on Piazza Santa Maria Novella
hotels.take: A small townhouse on Piazza Santa Maria Novella, with nearly everything that matters on foot. It feels less like a hotel and more like staying with a friend who has excellent taste. Plan one evening around the rooftop at aperitivo hour.

hotels.name: Collegio alla Querce
hotels.alt: The gardens at Collegio alla Querce in the hills above Florence
hotels.take: A former school in the hills, about a 30-minute walk from the center, with the whole city laid out below almost every room. I’ve stayed here, so I can tell you exactly which rooms face the Duomo.

hotels.name: Borgo Pignano Florence
hotels.alt: Borgo Pignano’s city house in Florence
hotels.take: The city house from the family behind Borgo Pignano, one of my favorite estates in Tuscany. Same calm, same eye for detail, on a smaller and more personal scale. It pairs beautifully with a few nights at the estate afterward.

hotels.name: Villa San Michele
hotels.alt: Belmond Villa San Michele, a former monastery on the Fiesole hillside above Florence
hotels.take: A 15th-century former monastery on the Fiesole hillside, recently renovated, with the best views in Florence. Terraces step down the slope and a shuttle takes you into town. Go spring through fall, when the terraces are the point.
